knownIssues.title: Instrument cluster / speedometer failure
knownIssues.description: Speedometer and warning lights fail from cracked solder joints on the cluster PCB, typically from ~40,000 km; legal/practical concern, not engine safety.

fixes.steps: 1) Confirm stuck/erratic needle or dead warning lights. 2) Tools: soldering iron, fine solder, multimeter, small screwdrivers. 3) Remove cluster, resolder cracked PCB joints. 4) Refit and check speedo sweep and lights. 5) DIY if comfortable soldering; escalate if stepper motor failed.

fixes.summary: Replace with a compatible cluster from another year or model
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm resolder is impractical or fault keeps returning. 2) Tools: compatible used/aftermarket cluster, adapter if needed. 3) Swap cluster and reconnect loom. 4) Verify speedo, odometer and lights on a short ride. 5) Escalate only if wiring loom is damaged.

knownIssues.title: Fragile electrical system and connector corrosion
knownIssues.description: Corroded connectors and wiring cause intermittent lights, indicators or no-start, worse with damp storage; can leave the bike temporarily unrideable.

fixes.summary: Inspect and repair corroded or damaged wiring and connectors
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm faults that change when wiggling connectors. 2) Tools: multimeter, contact cleaner, dielectric grease, crimps. 3) Clean earths/connectors; repair damaged wiring. 4) Recheck continuity and symptom over several cycles. 5) DIY with basic tools; escalate for main-harness replacement.

knownIssues.title: Excessive vibration at higher engine speed
knownIssues.description: Single-cylinder vibration loosens fasteners and fatigues mounts over time; inherent to the design, but ignored fasteners can be lost.

fixes.summary: Check and retighten fasteners, inspect mounts
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm loose panels, mirrors or brackets after a fast ride. 2) Tools: metric socket set, thread-locker. 3) Retighten fasteners; inspect rubber mounts. 4) Ride again and confirm no new rattles. 5) Escalate only if a mount is cracked or an insert stripped.

knownIssues.title: Carburettor gumming with poor-quality or stale fuel
knownIssues.description: Stale or poor fuel gums the carburettor, causing rough idle, hesitation or stalling, especially after the bike sits unused.

fixes.summary: Clean the carburettor and fuel system
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm rough idle/hesitation and residue in the float bowl. 2) Tools: carb cleaner, jet kit, bowl gasket, fresh fuel. 3) Clean jets/passages; flush tank and line. 4) Verify smooth idle and throttle response. 5) DIY for a single carb; escalate if mixture screws are damaged.

fixes.summary: Use quality fuel and fit an inline fuel filter
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm the bike is sound and the issue is fuel quality. 2) Tools: inline fuel filter, fresh fuel. 3) Fit filter between tank and carb; use reputable fuel. 4) Confirm rough running does not return over weeks. 5) No workshop escalation needed.

knownIssues.title: Limited performance for sustained high-speed or long-distance use
knownIssues.description: As a 125cc single, top speed is roughly 80-100 km/h; better for urban/short trips than sustained motorway use - usage limit, not a fault.

fixes.summary: Match usage to the bike's power class
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm town power is fine but motorway/pillion use feels strained. 2) Tools: none - riding-pattern change. 3) Prefer urban/secondary routes and realistic trip pacing. 4) Confirm expectations match adjusted routes. 5) No escalation - not a repairable defect.
